title: Utilizing AI for psychedelic textures in my blinking adventure game
author: SWEYET
selftext:
I ran an early version of generative AI on my development machine to create alternative versions of the textures in the game. Blinking is a mechanic of the game, sometimes things change on blinks. One of those things is swapping a texture for an AI distorted version of it.

To get the alternative textures I developed a custom app to slice up the texturemaps and generate the alternatives. I think early models have this great ghost-like quality where you can feel the combination of human experience going into them, I cant help but see it as anything other than Jung's idea of the the collective unconscious.

I have unfortunately been having a lot of pushback for AI integration into the game, journalists declining to cover due to worry about how their readers will perceive it.  Occasional negative comments depending on the sub, etc. Some developers i've spoken to have said i shouldnt disclose the AI usage, but i think it's a very interesting tool.  

Here's the link if you're keen to check it out the demo or wishlist, it's coming out next month so any support is greatly appreciated [https://store.steampowered.com/app/3063200/SWEYETetc/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3063200/SWEYETetc/) :) 

Video might not be the most engaging, but i think it shows the concept the clearest.

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body:
Oh this is fascinating! good stuff.

The aesthetic feels like it comes from the early internet days in the best way possible. Good luck with the launch!

The visual style of the game totally stands out If you can find a way to promote it so it reads as visually discernible on TikTok/Instagram Reels/YouTube shorts, I think you could have the kind of success a game like [Funi Raccoon Game](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3599690/Funi_Raccoon_Game/) has seen. It's on a similar plane of style

One note on the description itself: you should surface the fact that you're innovating on the eye tracking-based gameplay. Right now you almost sound apologetic about it. You underline *and* italicize the word "optional" as if it's a drawback. But I'd bet your original intent was full of excitement at being able to interact with your screen that naturally, so imo you should lean into it. Your game feels like it's promising the ability to dream while wide awake, and the eye tracking is how you actually deliver that one-of-a-kind experience.

For a reference, look at how the co-op game Meowgic (link: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4252290/Meowgic/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4252290/Meowgic/)) handles it. The voice-based control scheme is one where you you cast spells by shouting into the mic. The description puts this at the beginning: "A co-op fantasy adventure where your voice is magic. Play as cat wizards, cast spells by shouting into your mic, explore fairy-tale worlds, fight monsters, and return to your hot-air balloon loaded with loot."

You have the same opportunity with real-life blinking and eye movements in your game.

A smaller point on the thumbnail of your game: the text is set too close together, which makes it hard to read. I get that the stylistic choice was probably to layer that psychedelic texture over the words, but it ends up looking blurry and a little low quality. Giving the letters some breathing room would ensure you don't sacrifice legibility for style.

And finally, of everything in your one-liner and thumbnail on your steam page the most interesting and uncommon word is "dreamscape." I've found in my writing career, that if you can insert a set of 1-3 words max (and ideally forming a phrase with words directly adjacent to each other) in your main thesis, people will more easily remember you by that mimetic term you coined as being associated with your project you'e promoting. The word dreamscape is an awesome candidate for this because it's both a noun and also has some strong culturally relevant connotations (like vaporwave, Surrealism, Ethereal, subconscious / inner mind, almost like Inception). It's also an underused word that a lot of people will still understand

Last thing - how do you pronounce the name? It's not obvious from the spelling

This is one of the more unique applications of AI I've seen in creating new visual ideas, so congrats!

I kinda like the word soup going into this idea that there's a full title but everyone just goes by (etc.). As for the game pronunciation, i'll never correct anyone but lately i've just been calling it "sweet". My next commercial title will certainly have a more straightforward name though. 

As for the dreamscape bits, is the suggestion that i use dreamscape across more things, posts, adverts, etc. to take ownership of it, or that i work out a simple tagline i can put alongside it more?
